# konnect_ai_cost_export_schedule (Resource)

AICostExportSchedule Resource

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "konnect_ai_cost_export_schedule" "my_aicostexportschedule" {
  cadence     = "weekly"
  compression = "gzip"
  dataset     = "focus"
  filters     = "{ \"see\": \"documentation\" }"
  focus = {
    charge_period = "day"
    tag_keys = [
      "..."
    ]
    version = "1.4"
  }
  format = "csv"
  labels = {
    key = "value"
  }
  name      = "...my_name..."
  status    = "active"
  time_zone = "UTC"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cadence` (String) The length of each period, which sets the range of each export.

A replacement can't change it.
possible known values include one of ["daily", "weekly", "monthly"]; Requires replacement if changed.
- `compression` (String) How each export's data files are compressed.

`none` or `gzip` for `csv`, and `zstd` for `parquet`.
possible known values include one of ["none", "gzip", "zstd"]
- `dataset` (String) The data that each export holds. possible known values include one of ["usage_events", "focus"]
- `format` (String) The file format of each export's data files. possible known values include one of ["parquet", "csv"]
- `name` (String) A human-readable name for the schedule.

1 to 100 characters after the server removes leading and trailing whitespace.

### Optional

- `filters` (String) Filters that select the events to export, with the same fields, operators, and shape as the `filters` of `POST /v1/ai-cost-management/events/query`. Every filter must match.

Defaults to `{}`.
Parsed as JSON.
- `focus` (Attributes) The FOCUS options of each export.

Required when `dataset` is `focus`, and isn't accepted for any other dataset. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--focus))
- `labels` (Map of String) Key-value metadata on the schedule. The schedule list can filter by label. Each export that the schedule creates copies the labels as they are at that moment.
- `status` (String) Whether the schedule creates exports.

Defaults to `active`, so a replacement that omits `status` resumes a paused schedule.
possible known values include one of ["active", "paused"]; Default: "active"
- `time_zone` (String) The IANA time zone in which the periods start. Each export that the schedule creates has this `time_zone`.

An IANA time zone name as the time zone database spells it, such as `Europe/Budapest`. Offsets such as `+02:00` aren't accepted. A replacement can't change it, so a replacement of a schedule whose `time_zone` isn't `UTC` must repeat it. Defaults to `UTC`.
Default: "UTC"; Requires replacement if changed.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) An ISO-8601 timestamp representation of entity creation date.
- `id` (String) Contains a unique identifier used for this resource.
- `next_run_at` (String) When the period in progress ends and the schedule creates its export, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC. That export starts 6 hours later, so that events that arrive late can be stored first.

`null` while the schedule is `paused`. It's in the past while a run is late.
- `updated_at` (String) An ISO-8601 timestamp representation of entity update date.

<a id="nestedatt--focus"></a>
### Nested Schema for `focus`

Required:

- `version` (String) The FOCUS version of the files, which decides what their cost columns hold. possible known values include one of ["1.3", "1.4"]

Optional:

- `charge_period` (String) The length of each row's charge period.

Defaults to `day`.
possible known values include one of ["day", "hour"]; Default: "day"
- `tag_keys` (List of String) Tag keys whose values split the rows. Events with different values for a named key, or without the key, go into different rows. A row's `Tags` column holds the named keys that its events carry, with their values. A key with a different value for every agent session or CI run, such as `agent-session` or `ci-run`, makes about one row per session or run.

At most 64 keys, each listed once and following the tag key rules: 1 to 128 characters, each a lowercase ASCII letter, a digit, `.`, `_`, or `-`. Defaults to `[]`.
Default: []

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = konnect_ai_cost_export_schedule.my_konnect_ai_cost_export_schedule
  id = "5f9fd312-a987-4628-b4c5-bb4f4fddd5f7"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import konnect_ai_cost_export_schedule.my_konnect_ai_cost_export_schedule "5f9fd312-a987-4628-b4c5-bb4f4fddd5f7"
```
